correctness.rationale: The polynomial identity F=s^3−3st proves the first-level and three-branch mod-nine classification. In the branch (1,0,0), exact expansion gives F−1=9H and ∂H/∂a≡1 mod 3, yielding precisely 3^{2k−1} solutions per surviving mod-three class for every k≥2. All three derivatives of F are divisible by 3, so every reduction fiber has 0 or 27 points; total counts force exactly one third of level-k solutions to lift. Direct enumeration passed 18 selected prime-power cases and three lifting transitions. Finite data are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new quantified claim is the exact, persistent singular lifting sieve for the fixed r=1 norm-one equation over Z/3^kZ. Dutto–Murru (2022) work over finite fields; Seck–Nitaj (2024) prove prime-power cardinalities only when p≡1 mod 3; , Nitaj–Seck (2024) assumes prime factors different from three, and Murru–Saettone (2018) use a noncube parameter. None of these inspected statements implies the three surviving mod-three classes, their exact higher fibers, or the 1/3-to-27 lifting sieve. Searches of external mathematics pages and indexed mathematical findings yielded no equivalent explicit claim. General ramified norm-group theory remains a genuine possible implicit-cover risk.
residual_risks: General local-algebra norm-kernel formulas for non-étale cubic orders may already imply the exact result implicitly.

value.rationale: The ramified 3-adic norm-one problem is a natural omitted case of the existing cubic Pell prime-power counting theory. Beyond counts, the result identifies every surviving first-level residue class and an exact non-surjective reduction law at all depths, exposing a persistent failure of usual smooth Hensel lifting. This is a structural infinite-family classification of local arithmetic, not an arbitrary modular slice or routine finite check.
